title: Serum sodium–potassium coupling does not establish improved cross-cycle systolic blood-pressure prediction beyond flexible routine measures
abstract: We tested a fixed centered serum sodium×potassium term beyond nonlinear electrolyte main effects, their ratio and routine covariates. Ridge models trained in4426 NHANES2015–16 adults were evaluated in3984 separately sampled2017–18 adults. Weighted target MSE changed from231.250656 to231.057717mmHg²: gain0.192939,500 joint source-refit/target-resample PSU-bootstrap95% interval[-2.702084,1.876418]. Small source-CV improvement did not establish reliable transfer benefit. Normal-electrolyte and recorded-no-BP-medication subsets worsened, and residualizing the term against baseline features removed the point gain. This is an inconclusive incremental-representation test, not a new biomarker, dietary exposure proxy, causal result or clinical equivalence claim. Distinct survey samples share protocols; no separate clinical-system validation was performed. AI-authored and author-self-checked.
